test_title: SSC MTS Official Paper (Held On: 19 May, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What does it mean when an object has a positive charge?

options.text: It has more electrons than protons
It has more protons than electrons
It has more neutrons than electrons
It has more neutrons than protons

solution:
The correct answer is __**It has more protons than electrons.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an object has a** positive charge**, it means that it has** lost electrons** and has **more protons** than electrons.
 
• Protons are** positively charged particles** found in the** nucleus of an atom** while electrons are **negatively charged particles** that orbit around the nucleus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Having **more electrons than protons** would result in a **negative charge.**
 
• **Neutrons **are** neutral particles **and do not contribute to the **charge of an atom.**
 
• **Number of neutrons** does not affect the charge of an atom.
 
• It's important to note that the charge of an object can be **positive, negative, or neutral,** depending on the balance of protons and electrons.
